placements.quote: The NEMO-3 detector, which had been operating in the Modane Underground Laboratory from 2003 to 2010, was designed to search for neutrinoless double β (0νββ) decay.

isotope.quote: The main isotope used to search for 0νββ decays is 100 Mo with a total mass of 6.914 kg.

isotope_mass.quote: The main isotope used to search for 0νββ decays is 100 Mo with a total mass of 6.914 kg.

magnetic_field.quote: A solenoidal magnet surrounding the detector provides a magnetic field of 25 G

summary.plain: A drum of thin foils holding the decaying atoms, ringed by thousands of gas-filled tracking cells and blocks of plastic scintillator. It sees each electron's path and energy, so it can tell a real decay from background.
summary.technical: Cylinder with 20 sectors of source foils (100Mo 6.914 kg, 96.5 % enriched) between two Geiger-mode tracking volumes (6180 open drift cells) and plastic-scintillator walls read by PMTs; 25 G solenoid; 19 cm iron shield and borated-water neutron shield.

technology.quote: The thin source foils with a density of 40–60 mg/cm2 containing the active double β decay isotope are surrounded by a tracking detector comprising open drift cells and a calorimeter composed of plastic scintillators.
technology.value: Thin double-beta source foils surrounded by a gaseous tracking detector of open drift cells operating in Geiger mode and a calorimeter of plastic scintillators, inside a solenoid and a low-radioactivity shield
